name: Save-Data header
plain: Request header showing the person turned on data saving.
meaning: Save-Data: on indicates Lite mode on a metered or slow connection, often in lower-income or roaming contexts. Sites should send lighter pages.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can see that you turned on data saving, in Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet
limits.user_action: You turn on Data saver or Lite mode, then browse
can: See a Save-Data flag on each request when you have data saving on
Send smaller images and lighter pages
Guess you are on a slow or paid data plan
cannot: See anything if you have not turned data saving on
See your income, plan or provider, though a site may guess
limits.reach_label: A single on or off flag
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet only. Firefox and Safari, including all iPhone browsers, do not send it.

story.what_it_is: A header that tells a site you turned on data saving, so it can send less.
story.for_you: You never see the header. If you turned on Data Saver, many sites send smaller images, skip auto video or simplify the page. Your data plan lasts longer.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to cut costs and speed up pages for people on limited data. It is easy to support. It also tells the server a small thing about a user, which can add to a fingerprint.

use_cases.example: A news site sends text and small images only when Data Saver is on, so a reader on prepaid data can read more articles.
A video site starts at low quality and disables auto play for visitors who sent the data saving header.
A store shows fewer product photos on first load for shoppers who ask to save data.
A browser game portal delays the loading of trailers and keeps only the playable game for users who save data.
A social site skips auto playing clips in the feed for people with Data Saver.
A learning platform sends lighter lessons to students on limited mobile plans.
An ad server serves a lighter ad format when the header is on, so the page loads in time.
